── 4. does terrain slope feed the collision? ──
no. step() integrates x,z with velocity alone (physics.js:184-187); the ground is applied AFTER,
as a height the hull is locked to (physics.js:190-206: groundY=platformAt, hard clamp y>=groundH),
slope enters only as a gravity projection (physics.js:171-179) and a visual limb tilt clamped at
0.40 rad (physics.js:228-232); the only positional blockers iterated are collider discs (physics.js:246-257)
plus the r=1180 clamp (physics.js:273-274). Standing-start climb test: throttle 10.5 (physics.js:113),
gravity term max G*0.85 = 3.153 m/s^2 (physics.js:3,178) < 10.5 for ANY slope -> no slope stops the rover;
a slope-only rampart is therefore NOT a barrier. A slope can only make the far side unrecoverable,
which is exactly A5 (git 67ec15a/30862f8 notes: 62-67 deg face, no driving out).

option (a) seal pitch: replay of old ring seals per sealCheck={"closed":true,"holes":0,"widest_m":0} at 100 clasts (~pitch 7.26 m).
